prompt_c2:
You are a streetscape inventory annotator. Look ONLY at the uploaded streetscape image.
Return JSON ONLY. No markdown, no commentary, no reasoning.
 Task: record what is visible in the scene. Do not score, do not give design advice.
 Schema:
{
"road_type": "highway|arterial|neighborhood_street|alley|plaza|unclear",
"elements": {
"sidewalk": "true|false|unclear",
"bike_lane": "true|false|unclear",
"seating": "true|false|unclear",
"shade_trees": "none|few|many|unclear",
"curb_ramp": "true|false|unclear",
"tactile_paving": "true|false|unclear",
"pedestrian_crossing": "true|false|unclear",
"street_lighting": "true|false|unclear",
"greenery": "none|low|medium|high|unclear",
"vehicle_traffic": "none|light|heavy|unclear",
"bus_stop": "true|false|unclear"
},
"issues": ["no_seating", "little_shade", "no_bike_lane", "poor_accessibility", "narrow_sidewalk", "no_crossing", "high_traffic_exposure"],
"brief": "One or two English sentences describing the visible street scene."
}
 Rules:
- If an element is not clearly visible, use "unclear". Do not guess.
- "issues" may only list problems that are visible. Use [] if none.
- "brief" must mention concrete objects (sidewalk, trees, lanes, benches, ramps, etc.).

Article 59 Highway operating enterprises shall each year set aside an appropriate proportion of toll revenue exclusively for highway maintenance, so that the highway meets the requirements specified in paragraph 1 of Article 25 of these Regulations during the operating period. The provincial competent department for transportation shall, six months before the expiration of the operating period of an operating toll highway, organize appraisal and acceptance of the highway. If, upon acceptance, the highway does not meet the requirements of the preceding paragraph, the highway operating enterprise shall, within a prescribed time limit, take maintenance measures to bring it up to the required standard, or the highway maintenance management institution shall carry out maintenance on its behalf, with maintenance costs borne by the highway operating enterprise. Article 60 The setting of toll lanes shall meet the needs of traffic flow and facilitate vehicle passage. Toll stations shall open all toll lanes to ensure smooth highway traffic. Toll lanes shall not be closed without authorization. Toll station staff shall hold certificates to work, wear uniform insignia, collect tolls in accordance with law, and provide civilized and efficient services. Article 61 Vehicles entering the toll station area shall obey management, actively pay vehicle tolls, and shall not refuse to pay or force their way through; they shall not intentionally block toll lanes and affect the smooth operation of toll highways. No unit or individual may move or damage toll stations or their ancillary facilities without authorization. Chapter VIII Legal Liability Article 62 Where highway construction entities, survey and design entities, construction entities, or supervision entities violate the provisions of Article 18, Article 20, or Article 22 of these Regulations, the competent department for transportation or other relevant departments shall impose penalties in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations. Article 63 Where, in violation of paragraph 2 of Article 34 of these Regulations, buildings or structures are constructed or expanded, the competent department for transportation shall order removal within a prescribed time limit and may impose a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan and not more than 50,000 yuan; if removal is not made within the time limit, the competent department for transportation shall remove them, and the relevant expenses shall be borne by the builder or constructor. As a city streetscape evaluation expert, please analyze the uploaded streetscape image based on the specified persona perspective and evaluation indicators, and return a JSON result.
 Persona Selection
Road User Type
- All Road Users
- Pedestrians
- Cyclists
- Drivers
Socially Vulnerable Groups
- All Social Groups
- Persons with Disabilities
- Adolescents (<18)
- Older Adults (≥60)
Current Selection:
All Road Users; All Social Groups
 Indicator Selection
Justice
- Equity
- Fairness
- Accessibility
Safety
Livability
Sustainability
Aesthetics
Comfort
- Thermal Comfort
- Physical Comfort
- Psychological Comfort
Walkability
Bikeability
Selected Indicators:
Justice; Safety; Livability; Sustainability; Aesthetics; Comfort; Walkability
 1. Evaluation Dimensions
Justice: Analyze whether the environment fairly distributes spatial resources, including Equity (rationality of asset distribution), Fairness (non-discriminatory rules), and Accessibility (barrier-free physical design).
Comfort: Analyze physical perception at a micro-scale, including Thermal Comfort (shade/vegetation), Physical Comfort (paving/seating), and Psychological Comfort (noise/crowding).
Core Indicators: Safety, Livability, Sustainability, Aesthetics, Walkability, and Bikeability.
 2. Persona Perspective Requirements:
The analysis must strictly adhere to the persona's characteristics. For example:
Persons with Disabilities: Focus on curb ramps, continuity of tactile paving (blind tracks), and physical obstacles.
Elderly: Focus on resting facilities, slope gradients, and summer shade.
Teenagers: Focus on traffic calming measures and social surveillance (Eyes on the street).
 3. How to use the image vs retrieved knowledge:
- The IMAGE is the primary evidence. Score only what is visible or reasonably inferable from the photo.
- Section 6 provides retrieved guidelines and research. Use them to interpret the image (what the scene should provide for this persona/indicators), not to invent objects that are not in the photo.
- If retrieved text conflicts with the image, trust the image and say so in the explanation.
- Explanations must cite specific visible objects (benches, ramps, tree shade, lane markings, etc.). When a guideline is used, briefly connect it to those objects.

Purpose of Formulation Under the macro guidance of the “General Provisions,” these Detailed Rules aim at the refined construction of Suzhou’s urban roads, and are expanded and implemented from four directions: human-oriented, quality-oriented, distinctive, and intelligent. They interpret the refined construction of Suzhou’s urban roads in the form of colorful labels, and create urban colorful roads unique to Suzhou. ➢ Human-oriented: Starting from the users of Suzhou’s urban roads, and taking the public’s experience of urban road space as the benchmark, fully consider the comfort, safety, and convenience of public activities, and realize the value shift from “vehicle-centered” to “people-centered.” ➢ Quality-oriented: Vigorously improve the travel quality of people and vehicle traffic in Suzhou, and emphasize the public space function of roads. Appropriately raise the standards for urban road design, construction, and maintenance, extend road service life, and improve users’ comfort of experience. Reflect a road construction level of high appearance and high standards, with attention to detail and control. ➢ Distinctive: Adapt measures to local conditions, and through the embedding of Suzhou-style elements and the creation of road characteristic scenes, highlight Suzhou’s distinctive urban character of integration between tradition and modernity, so that urban roads become an important carrier and display space for the “Jiangnan culture” brand, and continue the city’s historical and cultural lineage. ➢ Intelligent: Deploy intelligent sensing devices along the roadside, together with cloud service platforms, computing and communication facilities, and through data technologies such as autonomous driving and vehicle-road coordination, realize a travel experience of deep interaction among people, vehicles, and road space, assist safe driving and autonomous driving, and create demonstration roads with Suzhou’s smart-city characteristics. 2. Vehicle Traffic System 2 Vehicle Traffic System 2.1 Vehicle Traffic Space Scale The longitudinal and transverse road space occupied by vehicular traffic is referred to as vehicle traffic space. Generally speaking, vehicle traffic space includes carriageways, bus-only lanes, medians, and roadside parking lanes. Figure 2.1-1 Components of Vehicle Traffic Space 2.1.1 Motor Vehicle Lane The width of a motor vehicle lane shall include the carriageway width and the curb lane widths on both sides. Where a single carriageway road or a three-carriageway road uses a central separator or double yellow lines to separate opposing traffic, the pavement width of the motor vehicle lane shall also include the width of the separator or double yellow lines. 1. Running Lane The width of a running lane is related to the road design speed. The recommended width for urban road running lanes is 3.25 m–3.5 m. 2. Two-Way Single Lane Where a lower-grade branch road is designed as a single lane permitting two-way travel, the width shall be 4.5 m. The subgrade width for sections with passing bays shall not be less than 6.5 m. 3. Bus-Only Lane The recommended width of a bus-only lane is 3.5 m. At bus stops, the lane width shall be 3 m. 27 Figure 2.1-2 Typical Lane Width Settings 2.1.2 Tidal Lane In response to the “tidal phenomenon” of traffic, lanes may be provided on road sections whose direction of travel can be changed according to traffic flow demand. In addition, the control center may monitor intersection conditions through instruments and, when appropriate, use remote control means to control signboards; where intersection signal controllers are connected in a computer network, they may also be identified through an automatic recognition system and automatically regulated. In terms of planning concept, shared roads emphasize people-centered design, serving pedestrians and providing convenience for urban residents, making them more willing to gather in shared-road spaces. Article 59 Highway operating enterprises shall each year set aside an appropriate proportion of toll revenue exclusively for highway maintenance, so that the highway meets the requirements specified in paragraph 1 of Article 25 of these Regulations during the operating period. The provincial competent department for transportation shall, six months before the expiration of the operating period of an operating toll highway, organize appraisal and acceptance of the highway. If, upon acceptance, the highway does not meet the requirements of the preceding paragraph, the highway operating enterprise shall, within a prescribed time limit, take maintenance measures to bring it up to the required standard, or the highway maintenance management institution shall carry out maintenance on its behalf, with maintenance costs borne by the highway operating enterprise. Article 60 The setting of toll lanes shall meet the needs of traffic flow and facilitate vehicle passage. Toll stations shall open all toll lanes to ensure smooth highway traffic. Toll lanes shall not be closed without authorization. Toll station staff shall hold certificates to work, wear uniform insignia, collect tolls in accordance with law, and provide civilized and efficient services. Article 61 Vehicles entering the toll station area shall obey management, actively pay vehicle tolls, and shall not refuse to pay or force their way through; they shall not intentionally block toll lanes and affect the smooth operation of toll highways. No unit or individual may move or damage toll stations or their ancillary facilities without authorization. Chapter VIII Legal Liability Article 62 Where highway construction entities, survey and design entities, construction entities, or supervision entities violate the provisions of Article 18, Article 20, or Article 22 of these Regulations, the competent department for transportation or other relevant departments shall impose penalties in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations. Article 63 Where, in violation of paragraph 2 of Article 34 of these Regulations, buildings or structures are constructed or expanded, the competent department for transportation shall order removal within a prescribed time limit and may impose a fine of not less than 5,000 yuan and not more than 50,000 yuan; if removal is not made within the time limit, the competent department for transportation shall remove them, and the relevant expenses shall be borne by the builder or constructor. Article 64 Where any of the following illegal acts occur, the competent department for transportation shall order cessation of the illegal act, correction within a prescribed time limit, and may impose the following penalties: (1) In violation of Article 36 of these Regulations, engaging in operations that endanger the safety of highways, highway bridges, highway tunnels, or highway ferries, a fine of not less than 1,000 yuan and not more than 30,000 yuan may be imposed. (2) In violation of items 1 and 2 of paragraph 1 of Article 37 of these Regulations, a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan and not more than 100,000 yuan shall be imposed.
